core_obligations: Part (1) (proof line 5331): the exactness of gr(A) -> gr(B) -> gr(C) is the exactness of the direct sum of the sequences gr^p(A) -> gr^p(B) -> gr^p(C), so the assertion is immediate from the definitions.

Part (3) by induction on the length of the filtrations (proof lines 5332-5351): with n the largest index for which one of F^nA, F^nB, F^nC is nonzero, the quotients A' = A/F^nA and its companions carry induced finite filtrations with gr(A) = F^nA plus gr(A'), so the induction hypothesis gives exactness of the sequences of quotients for p at least n; a commutative diagram of short exact sequences then produces exactness of A -> B -> C, which is the case p = n+1.
Parts (2) and (5) (proof line 5352): the assertion about the filtration steps is dual to (3), and the exactness of A -> B -> C follows from (2).
Part (4) (proof lines 5354-5361): the strictness of f : A -> B follows from the chain f(F^p A) = ker(F^p B -> F^p C) = f(A) intersected with F^p B, using (2) and (5), and the strictness of g is dual.
proof_roadmap: Read part (1) off the definition of the associated graded.
Induct on the length of the filtrations to get exactness of the quotients.
Get the exactness of the complex from the same diagram.
Derive strictness from the identifications of kernels.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a complex of filtered objects with finite filtrations whose associated graded is exact is itself exact, with exactness also of the filtration steps and of the successive quotients, and with both maps strict (statement lines 5311-5328). The proof is a complete argument: part (1) is read off the definitions, part (3) is proved by induction on the length of the filtrations with a commutative diagram of short exact sequences carrying the induction step (proof lines 5332-5351), the dual assertion for the filtration steps gives exactness of the complex, and strictness is obtained by identifying the image of each filtration step with the appropriate kernel (proof lines 5354-5361). The non-formal content is the induction and the strictness computation. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
